title: Google's homepage now has a sidebar for your AI searches
excerpt: It's for picking up your AI searches
content_html:
Google's homepage just got its biggest change in years, and it's all about AI

Published Nov 19, 2026, 7:49 PM EST

Timi is the news and deals reporter for Android Police, who has been reporting on technology since 2008. He has worked in tech retail and also the IT space, providing hardware and software support, which gives him a unique perspective on the tech that he covers. This allows him to effectively break down complex subjects into easy-to-read pieces that even casual readers can enjoy. Before joining Android Police, he was a news writer for XDA, where he eventually transitioned to covering deals. He also worked as an editor and reporter for Neowin, where he covered news and attended major tech events like CES. He also reviewed phones, tablets, PC products, and other devices. In addition, he also created video content for the Neowin YouTube channel.

Sign in to your Android Police account

The Google homepage used to be dead simple. And while it might seem fairly normal by today's standards, it was incredibly different from what the competition was doing at the time. And people really enjoyed that simplicity.

There was just one search bar with no other distractions like news or the weather that you'd see on Yahoo or AOL. Now, over time, Google has added to the Search page, but it has kept things as tame as possible.

That said, the Google homepage is getting one of its biggest changes yet, adding a new "collapsible sidebar" that will make it easier to see your AI searches. This update is now live on the web page if you want to check it out.

Might not be for everyone

9to5Google was quick to pick up on this change, highlighting a tweet on X from Robby Stein, who is the VP, Product at Google Search. Stein shares that this change is now rolling globally for Google Search on web and is something that tested well.

The goal is to allow users to continue their AI searches and come back to them, or, as Stein shares, "A much simpler way to pick up where you left off." If you head to the Google Search page and enter into AI Mode, you can see the new search bar pop up.

There's the option to open the sidebar, where you can create a New thread or Search through previous ones. Google has been pushing its AI efforts into all its products and services, so this was eventually going to happen.

While purists might be upset about this change, I think that Google did a pretty good job of making it optional. Plus, it doesn't disturb the classic layout of Google Search by much. Again, some will beg to differ, but it is what it is.

Naturally, if you don't want this to be a part of your experience, you can always just not enter into AI Mode. For most of my own searches, I rarely enable this. On mobile, though, it is a different story.

Will this eventually come to mobile?

There's a pretty good chance at some point that this feature will come to the mobile version of Android and iOS. Getting AI into as many hands as possible is top priority for Google, which means it would just make sense.

What do you think about this change? Is it something you're looking forward to using? Or does it not make any difference to your daily workflow? Let us know in the comments below.
